name: Code Cubicle 6.0
tagline: Where Builders ship from the Office Cubicle
about: **Where Builders Take Their Cubicles and Build** Code Cubicle 6.0 is back – bigger, bolder, and built for the next generation of **creators, coders, and problem-solvers**. For this edition, office cubicles become **innovation labs**, giving teams a space to pick a meaningful problem, experiment with ideas, and build something real. Whether you're building with **AI**, developing a product, designing a solution, or exploring something completely new, Code Cubicle 6.0 gives you the platform to turn your ideas into working solutions. ### WHAT TO EXPECT - Build and experiment with **real-world solutions**. - Collaborate with fellow **builders, creators, and innovators**. - Explore technologies including **AI, software, and emerging technologies**. - Showcase your solution through the **hackathon's evaluation rounds**. - Compete for the opportunity to reach the **Final Round** and be among the **top 3 teams**. **Bring an idea. Enter a cubicle. Build something that matters.**

eligibility.details:
- Students, developers, engineers, AI builders, and working professionals can participate.
- Participants can join individually or as part of a team.
- Each team can have **1–4 members**.
- Participants must complete the registration process before the deadline.
- Participants must be available to attend the **Final Round offline at Paytm, Noida** if selected.
- There are no specific academic or professional background requirements to participate.

themes.name: AI-Powered Intelligence for the Real World
themes.description:
Build AI systems that go beyond chatbots and demos to solve real-world problems using data, media, and edge intelligence. Create products that can collect and understand information, make intelligent decisions, search and reason over knowledge, process rich media, or operate locally where connectivity and latency matter.

The goal is simple: turn real-world data into actionable intelligence using AI.

problem_statements.name: AI-Powered Impact & Sustainability Media Platform
problem_statements.description: The challenge is to build an AI-powered media intelligence platform using Cloudinary that can understand field media, organize evidence by project, location, and timeline, and help teams turn visual data into reliable insights and impact stories.

problem_statements.name: AI-Powered Data Intelligence Platform
problem_statements.description: The challenge is to build an AI-powered data intelligence platform where users can describe what they need in plain English. The AI should understand the request, dynamically create and execute an appropriate data-collection workflow, gather information from permitted sources, process and validate the data, and present the results through a centralized dashboard.

problem_statements.name: AI-Powered Edge Memory & Intelligence Platform
problem_statements.description: The challenge is to build an AI-powered edge intelligence platform that uses Qdrant Edge to provide local semantic memory and retrieval, while intelligently managing the relationship between on-device data and centralized cloud knowledge.

announcements.title: Code Cubicle 6.0: Online Round Shortlist Announced
announcements.description:
Hi Participants,

We’re excited to share that we have now shortlisted around 400 teams for the Online Round of Code Cubicle 6.0.

These are the final teams selected as of now. We may open additional slots and select more teams if required, but for the current stage, this is the shortlist we’re proceeding with.

How did we select the teams?

We wanted to keep the selection process as transparent and consistent as possible.

For this round, we decided to use GitHub as the primary and only evaluation source. While we initially considered other platforms such as LinkedIn, we found that LinkedIn activity varied significantly across participants and did not provide a consistent basis for evaluating student developers. Some participants may have limited or no activity on LinkedIn despite being active builders.

GitHub, on the other hand, is where developers typically showcase their code, projects, contributions, and technical work. Therefore, to maintain a consistent evaluation methodology across all participants, we based the shortlist entirely on publicly available GitHub information.

The evaluation considered factors such as:
* Contributions over the last year
* Recent GitHub activity
* Recently pushed repositories
* README presence and documentation
* Repository descriptions
* Stars and forks
* Programming language breadth
* Public profile activity
* Overall evidence of project work
* Team composition and depth

For team scoring, we considered the strength of the strongest member, the top two members, and the overall team average, rather than simply rewarding larger teams.

Please also keep in mind that a GitHub-based evaluation cannot capture everything a developer has done. Private contributions, internships, research, hackathon achievements, or work outside GitHub may not be visible through this methodology. We therefore did not make assumptions about achievements that could not be verified through the available GitHub data.

Selection Methodology & Results:
We’re sharing the results sheet along with the methodology used for the evaluation so that the process is as transparent as possible:

Results + Methodology:
https://docs.google.com/spreadsheets/d/1nxZF2XUeYhFqIMxV8Y6eIvINZ0G4Zr5RYQ9h0-pqO34/edit?usp=sharing

A request regarding individual requests:

We understand that some participants may have questions about their selection. However, we request that you please do not DM the team asking for reconsideration, manual selection, or individual profile reviews.

We simply don’t have the bandwidth to handle individual selection requests, and making exceptions would also make it difficult to maintain a consistent process for everyone.

We’ve tried to make the methodology as transparent as possible and have shared the basis on which the selections were made.

What happens next?
If your team has been shortlisted, you will soon receive a separate email with details about the dedicated Online Round participants group. Please keep an eye on your inbox and make sure you join the group once you receive the invitation.

We’ll also share the problem statements and further Online Round instructions soon.

For those who have been selected - congratulations, and we’ll see you in the Online Round.

For everyone else, thank you for participating and for being part of Code Cubicle 6.0. We genuinely appreciate the interest and effort from everyone who registered.

Best,
Team Geek Room

rules:
### 1. Participation
- Participants can participate individually or in teams.
- Each team can have a maximum of 4 members.
- All participants must provide accurate information during registration.
- Participants are responsible for completing their registration before the deadline.

### 2. Team Formation
- Participants can create or join a team during the Team Formation phase.
- Each participant can be part of only one team.

### 3. Project & Submission
- Projects must be built by the participating team.
- Teams should submit their own original work.
- Participants may use open-source tools, libraries, APIs, and AI tools where applicable.
- Any external resources or third-party work used in the project should be properly credited.

### 4. Selection
- Teams will be evaluated based on their overall profile, including their GitHub and LinkedIn profiles.
- Selected teams will be invited to the Final Round.
- The organizers' decision regarding team selection will be final.

### 5. Final Round
- Selected teams must be available to attend the Final Round offline at Paytm, Noida.
- Teams must present and demonstrate their project during the Final Round.
- The final winners will be selected by the hackathon jury based on the evaluation criteria.

### 6. Code of Conduct
- Participants are expected to behave respectfully towards other participants, organizers, mentors, and judges.
- Any form of cheating, plagiarism, harassment, or misconduct may result in disqualification.
- The organizers reserve the right to disqualify any participant or team that violates the rules.

### 7. General
- The organizers reserve the right to modify the schedule or rules if required.
- Participants are responsible for checking official hackathon updates and announcements.
- By participating in the hackathon, participants agree to follow these rules and guidelines.
